answer: Give every identity a slow start: a newcomer begins with zero weight, like a juniper seedling, and gains influence only by submitting small, spaced proofs of useful work across many consecutive epochs. Each proof must arrive in its own window, so a burst of activity earns nothing extra. A Sybil farmer's voyage then turns expensive: every puppet must be kept alive and working for weeks before it counts, and any gap resets its progress, while the echo of one honest agent's steady record keeps compounding. Attackers pay in sustained time, not one cheap registration.
